Drywall & Ceiling Repair in Walnut Creek, CA

Walnut Creek runs heavily to homes built between the mid-1950s and the late 1970s, and that vintage has a predictable set of drywall problems: hairline cracks marching out from door headers, nail pops down hallway walls, and the wall-to-ceiling joint opening up a little more every summer as the frame moves.

We repair, texture-match and finish so the patch stops being visible — which matters more here than most places, because so much of the local housing stock has smooth or lightly textured walls where a sloppy blend shows from across the room.

What drywall work looks like in Walnut Creek

The split across town is real. West of Ygnacio Valley Road, around Parkmead and Walnut Heights, you get 1950s ranch homes with original board and hand-applied texture. Out toward Northgate and the Ygnacio Valley corridor the houses are newer, mostly orange peel and knockdown, and the common failure is seam cracking rather than damage. Downtown condos near Broadway Plaza are a third category again — shared walls, HOA rules, and repairs that have to be quiet and clean.

Housing note: Roughly two-thirds of Walnut Creek housing predates 1980, so asbestos testing before any popcorn ceiling work is standard rather than optional.

Drywall Repair

The bread-and-butter job in Walnut Creek: patch, blend, texture, prime, gone. Most single-room repairs are a one-day visit.

  • ▪ Stress cracks radiating from door and window corners in 1950s–70s ranch homes

  • ▪ Doorknob holes and moved-furniture damage
  • ▪ Cut-outs left open after plumbing or electrical work

Ceiling Repair

Ceilings show every flaw under Walnut Creek’s flat afternoon light. We float wide and match texture rather than dropping in an obvious square.

More on ceiling repair →
  • ▪ Wall-to-ceiling joint cracks taped properly instead of re-caulked
  • ▪ Sagging board re-screwed to framing before finishing
  • ▪ Second-floor bathroom leaks coming through the ceiling below
  • ▪ Can-light and fixture cut-outs closed cleanly
  • ▪ Knockdown and orange peel patterns matched overhead

Texture Matching

A structurally sound patch that does not match the texture still looks like a repair. This is the part most handymen skip.

Drywall questions from Walnut Creek homeowners

How quickly can you look at a drywall repair in Walnut Creek? +

Most Walnut Creek quote requests get a callback the same business day, and small repairs are usually scheduled within the week. Active leaks and open ceilings get moved up.

Do you work in Rossmoor and downtown condo buildings? +

Yes. Both come with rules — Rossmoor mutuals and downtown HOAs typically want notice, insurance on file, and work confined to set hours. We plan around that rather than showing up and finding out.

My Walnut Creek home is from 1965 and has a popcorn ceiling. Can you just scrape it? +

Not before it is tested. Acoustic ceilings applied before the early 1980s can contain asbestos, and a 1965 ceiling is squarely in that window. Testing is quick and cheap relative to the alternative.

How much does drywall repair cost? +

It depends far more on access, height and texture than on the size of the hole. A single small patch at standard ceiling height is the least expensive job we do; the same patch on a two-storey entry wall costs several times more because of staging and protection. We give written quotes before any work starts.

Can you match my existing wall texture? +

Yes — orange peel, knockdown, skip trowel, hand-troweled and Level 5 smooth. For unusual or hand-applied finishes we prepare a sample panel and get your sign-off before touching the visible wall. Where a blend genuinely will not disappear, we will tell you that re-texturing the whole wall is the better answer rather than leaving you with a patch you can see.

Do you paint after the repair? +

We finish, texture and prime every repair so it is ready for paint and the sheen matches. Final colour coats are usually best handled by your painter, who has your exact paint — but ask, because on small jobs we can often finish it out.

How long does a typical repair take? +

Joint compound has to dry between coats, so most repairs are one long day or two shorter visits. Anyone promising a finished, textured, invisible repair in ninety minutes is skipping a coat.
